# Constant-time code is written so that its running time does not depend on secret
# data, and a rewrite adds a runtime overlap check, a length check, and vector
# loads that nobody audited. Cryptographic packages are left alone unless
# LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC_CRYPTO is set. crypto/tls has a loop the wrapper would rewrite.

env GOEXPERIMENT=simd
env GOCACHE=$WORK/gocache
env LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC_LOG=$WORK/log
env LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC_DEBUG=1
env LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC_LOG_PKGS=crypto/tls
exec go build -toolexec=$LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC -o app .
! stdout .
! stderr .
cmp log log.want
exec ./app
cmp stdout want.out

# Opting in rewrites it. The build cache does not know about the variable, so
# the second build needs a cache of its own.
env LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC_CRYPTO=1
env GOCACHE=$WORK/gocache2
rm log
exec go build -toolexec=$LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC -o app .
grep '^rewrote [0-9]+ loop.s. in crypto/tls$' log
exec ./app
cmp stdout want.out

-- go.mod --
module example.com/app

go 1.27.1
-- main.go --
package main

import (
	"crypto/tls"
	"fmt"
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(tls.VersionName(tls.VersionTLS13))
}
-- want.out --
TLS 1.3
-- log.want --
skipped crypto/tls: cryptographic code is left alone (LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC_CRYPTO=1 rewrites it)
